data.name: Mujid
data.gender_notes: Mujid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who guides, helps, or shows the way. The name Mujid carries the meaning “Guide” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Mujid usually hope their child will grow to embody guide and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who seek to be a spiritual guide for others, helping them find their way through life's challenges
data.etymology: Mujid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guide.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mujid total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: مجيد
in_arabic.meaning: اسم الله الحسنى المجيد المالك للمجد كله
in_arabic.long_meaning: المجيد هو من أسماء الله الحسنى في الإسلام، ويعني المالك للمجد كله، الذي له المجد والكرامة في الدنيا والآخرة، وهو اسم الفاعل من مجد يمجده إذا عظمه وكرمه، ومنه قوله تعالى: واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا * ومن الليل فاسجد له وسبحه ليلا طويلا

in_urdu.name: مجید
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ تعالی کا نام، مجید کا مطلب ہے شاندار
in_urdu.long_meaning: مجید اللہ تعالی کے خوبصورت ناموں میں سے ایک ہے، جو تمام عزت و احترام کا مالک ہے، یہ نام اللہ تعالی کی شان و عظمت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، اور یہ صفت مجید سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے عزت دینے والا یا شاندار

in_hindi.name: मुजीद
in_hindi.meaning: मुजीद का अर्थ है ईश्वर की विशेषता
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुजीद इस्लामी परंपरा में एक महत्वपूर्ण नाम है, जिसका अर्थ है ईश्वर की विशेषता या ईश्वर का गुण होना, यह नाम अरबी मूल से निकला है और इसका उपयोग मुस्लिम समुदाय में व्यापक रूप से किया जाता है

in_pashto.name: مجيد
in_pashto.meaning: د الله جل جلاله نوم، مجيد د عزت معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: مجيد د الله پاک د نومو څخه يو دی، چي د عزت او شان د مالک دی، دا نوم د الله پاک د قدرت او حکمت څرګندوي، او د مجید صفت څخه مشتق شوی دی، چي معنی یې د عزت ورکونکی دی

in_english.name: Mujid
in_english.meaning: One of Allah's names, means glorious and honored
in_english.long_meaning: Mujid is one of the beautiful names of Allah in Islam, meaning the glorious and honored one, derived from the Arabic root 'M-J-D' which connotes the idea of glory, honor, and praise, reflecting the attribute of Allah who is the owner of all glory and dignity

data.cultural_impact: The name Mujid carries a strong positive connotation in the Islamic cultural context. In various Islamic literature, folklores, and tales, a Mujid is often depicted as a wise and virtuous guide who shows the right path to the lost. This can apply to various spheres of life, including spiritual guidance, moral principles, and even navigational aid. The term has a deep-rooted significance in the collective Islamic consciousness, reminding us of the values of guidance, compassion, and helping those who are in need.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Mujid represents an embodiment of compassion, kindness, and enlightenment. It suggests an individual who is aware of the Divine Guidance and strives to help others find their way to self-discovery and spiritual growth. The name serves as an inspiration to live in harmony with the Divine Will, to help others, and ultimately, to lead a meaningful life filled with purpose and fulfillment. In essence, being called Mujid implies having a servants' heart that is always ready to extend a helping hand to those in need, both spiritually and materially, and to lead them towards their inherent spiritual growth and development.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Guide" symbolizes The one who guides, helps, or shows the way. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Mujid serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of guide.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah Wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 13, Page 536 The name Mujid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mujahed bin Bashr Al-Sulami, also known as Mujid Al-Din, was a prominent Sufi scholar and poet. He was born in Palestine and studied under Imam Al-Ghazali and other renowned scholars. Mujid Al-Din is famous for his poem 'Miftah Al-Jannah', which was a source of inspiration for many Sufis.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Suyuti's Tabaqat Al-Shafi'iyah, Volume 4, Page 220 The name Mujid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Mahmoud Al-Ansari, commonly known as Mujid Al-Din, was a Shafi'i jurist and scholar. He was born in Damascus and studied under Ibn Uthaymeen and Ibn Taymiyyah. Mujid Al-Din was renowned for his knowledge in Hadith and Fiqh and authored several books on these subjects.

modern_usage.modern_context: Mujid, meaning 'gracious' or 'blessed' in Arabic, is an increasingly popular Islamic name for children in modern contexts. As Western countries continue to embrace diversity and multiculturalism, more parents are choosing Islamic names for their children as a way to honor their heritage or explore new cultural traditions. Social media platforms like Pinterest, Instagram, and Facebook provide abundant resources and inspiration for those seeking unique and spiritual names for their children, with Mujid being a popular choice due to its meaningful and positive connotations. Many Muslim influencers and bloggers share their experiences of raising children with Islamic names, while Muslim communities and parenting groups on these platforms offer support and resources for families with similar values and practices. Overall, the trend towards Islamic names like Mujid reflects a growing interest in and appreciation for the rich cultural heritage and spiritual traditions of the Islamic world.
